claims.value: L2W l2_flags bitmask of ACOLITE's own masking steps
claims.note: Bits: SWIR threshold 0, cirrus 1, TOA threshold 2, negative 3, out-of-scene 4, VIIRS mixed 5, DEM shadow 6. The listed flags name no Sentinel-2 scene classification.
claims.quote: flag_exponent_swir=0 Bit index that will be used to store the SWIR threshold masking step (2**0). flag_exponent_cirrus=1 Bit index that will be used to store the cirrus masking step (2**1). flag_exponent_toa=2 Bit index that will be used to store the top-of-atmosphere threshold masking step (2**2). flag_exponent_negative=3 Bit index that will be used to store the negative retrievals masking step (2**3). flag_exponent_outofscene=4 Bit index that will be used to store the out-of-scene masking step (2**4). flag_exponent_mixed=5 Bit index that will be used to store the VIIRS mixed pixel masking step (2**5). flag_exponent_dem_shadow=6 Bit index that will be used to store the DEM shadow masking step (2**6).

claims.value: Non-water test: TOA reflectance above 0.0215 in the band nearest 1600 nm
claims.note: Defaults l2w_mask_wave=1600 and l2w_mask_threshold=0.0215. It is a single-band threshold, not a classification. A manual example raises it to 0.05.
claims.quote: l2w_mask_wave=1600 Wavelength (nm) for the non-water masking. The closest band will be selected. l2w_mask_threshold=0.0215 Threshold for the non-water masking. Pixels with ρt in the masking band above this threshold will be masked.

claims.value: Fixed DSF stores its single aerosol optical thickness in NetCDF global attributes
claims.note: A per-pixel aerosol layer is written only with dsf_write_aot_550=True. This records which aerosol value produced each scene.
claims.quote: dsf_write_aot_550=False Controls output of a per pixel (interpolated or resampled) aerosol optical thickness dataset. Note that in fixed processing this is also output as a single float in the NetCDF global attributes. Options: True/False

claims.value: Full download: one local .SAFE folder per scene, archives extracted first
claims.note: Input is a local path. ACOLITE extracts zip or tar inputs by default (extract_inputfile=True). The whole product must sit on local disk.
claims.quote: Scene or comma separated list of scenes to be processed. Full paths to the scene directory (Landsat bundle or Sentinel-2 .SAFE file) have to be specified. The comma separated list has to be on a single line. Automatic extraction of compressed files is supported, see also delete_extracted_input to remove the extracted files after processing.

claims.value: Sentinel-2 input must be Level-1C, not Level-2A
claims.note: Atmospheric correction starts from top-of-atmosphere data. A Level-2A surface reflectance product is not a valid input. The 20221114.0 manual carries the same instruction.
claims.quote: Sentinel-2 Provide the full path to the .SAFE file. Make sure you have a L1C TOA bundle, not a L2 SR bundle.

claims.value: The Sentinel-2 converter skips any product whose level is not Level-1C
claims.note: The level comes from PROCESSING_LEVEL in the product metadata. The Zarr converter has the same test on processing:level 'L1C' at line 73.
claims.quote:
if meta['PROCESSING_LEVEL'] != 'Level-1C':
            print('Processing of {} Sentinel-2 {} data not supported'.format(bundle, meta['PROCESSING_LEVEL']))

claims.note: It writes Sen2Cor reflectance as rhos_l2a datasets without ACOLITE correction. At commit ca477dd no caller of this Sentinel-2 function was found.
claims.quote: ## converts Sentinel-2 L2A Sen2Cor .SAFE bundle data to s2c_l2a NetCDF

claims.note: Defaults extract_zip=True and remove_zip=True unzip the archive and delete the zip. A product already on disk is not downloaded again.

claims.value: Sentinel-2 Zarr inputs may be HTTPS URLs read through GDAL /vsicurl
claims.note: Release 20260421.0 notes announce Zarr support. This is the Copernicus Zarr format, not an AWS GeoTIFF or SAFE route. It was not tested here.

claims.value: Region limit as south, west, north, east bounds in decimal degrees
claims.note: Setting limit. Without limit or polygon the full tile is processed. Default limit=None.
claims.quote: Comma separated list of the bounding box coordinates of the region of interest in decimal degrees in S,W,N,E order. If empty, and polygon=None the full scene will be processed.

claims.value: A polygon file, WKT, or GeoJSON string, whose envelope crops the scene by default
claims.note: With polygon_limit=False the full scene is processed and data kept for covered polygons.
claims.quote: A polygon file (e.g. geojson) specifying the bounding box for the region of interest. Alternatively a string in WKT or GeoJSON format can also be provided. If None, and limit is empty, the full scene will be processed. polygon_limit=True Whether to use the bounding envelope of the polygon file to crop the scene. If False, the full scene will be processed retaining data for the polygons covered by the scene. Options=True/False
claims.locator: Section 4.1 'General options', settings 'polygon=None' and 'polygon_limit=True', PDF page 21

claims.value: Optional clip to the polygon outline, off by default
claims.note: Default polygon_clip=False. In l1_convert.py line 685, clipped pixels become NaN in the top-of-atmosphere bands before atmospheric correction.
claims.quote: polygon_clip=False Whether to crop the subsetted scene using the polygon boundaries. Can be used for subsetting to non rectangular regions of interest. Options=True/False

claims.value: Each tile is processed on its own unless merge_tiles is set
claims.note: Default merge_tiles=False in config/defaults.txt line 37. Merging needs scenes from one orbit. Without merging there is no mosaic.
claims.quote: Controls whether inputfiles have to be merged before processing. Merging is only supported for scenes from the same orbit. Supported sensors are Landsat, Sentinel-2/MSI, PlanetScope, Sentinel-3/OLCI and MERIS, VIIRS, and PACE/OCI. If no region of interest is specified when merging projected data from Landsat, Sentinel-2 or PlanetScope, merge_full_tiles also has to be set. Options: True/False

claims.value: Unmerged outputs carry the MGRS tile code, merged outputs carry 'merged'
claims.note: The tile code enters the output name and the tile_code attribute. A merged output names no single tile.

claims.value: Merging tiles from two UTM zones reprojects them to the first tile's zone
claims.note: Shown in a manual example with four tiles in zones 32 and 33.
claims.quote: A settings file for a larger region of interest, merging four Sentinel-2 tiles from two different UTM zones (two from zone 33, two from zone 32). Note that the zone from the first tile (in this case 33) will be used as reference to reproject the other tiles before merging

claims.value: By default the output covers only the part of the region inside the tile
claims.note: Default extend_region=False. A water body across a tile edge would yield a partial output from each tile.
claims.quote: extend_region=False Controls whether the output file has to cover the entire limit or polygon, or whether it can be limited to the scene extent. Options: True/False

claims.value: Per-pixel surface reflectance rhos in NetCDF
claims.note: L1R files hold top-of-atmosphere rhot. L2R files hold rhos. L2W files hold requested parameters.
claims.quote: Level 2 outputs are surface level reflectance (ρs=Rrs⋅π) and derived products that are saved as geolocated datasets in a NetCDF file, and can be exported as PNG maps.

claims.value: L2W rhow is rhos with a SWIR non-water mask, and Rrs is rhow divided by pi
claims.note: Requested through l2w_parameters, for example rhow_* or Rrs_*.
claims.quote: rhow_*: ρw , the surface level reflectance for water pixels, with a SWIR based mask applied to non-water pixels. A wavelength can be specified, or the asterisk will be expanded to include all available wavelengths. Sensors: all sensors

claims.value: Optional GeoTIFF export of NetCDF datasets
claims.note: Settings l1r_export_geotiff, l2r_export_geotiff, and l2w_export_geotiff default to False.
claims.quote: Optionally the datasets from the NetCDF files can be output to GeoTIFF files if the original input data were in a projection supported by GeoTIFF, or if the data are reprojected within ACOLITE.

claims.value: GeoTIFF export writes one file per dataset
claims.note: File names append the dataset name to the NetCDF base name.
claims.quote: outfile = '{}_{}{}'.format(out, ds, '.tif')

claims.value: Four DSF aerosol modes: fixed, tiled, segmented, and experimental resolved
claims.note: Fixed gives one aerosol for the scene or subscene. Tiled uses about 6 by 6 km tiles. Segmented gives one value per lake polygon.
claims.quote: Four settings for the DSF are implemented: 1. A "fixed" τa option, which computes a single τa for the scene or subscene if limits for a ROI are provided. 2. A "tiled" τa option, which divides the full scene in approximately 6x6 km tiles, retrieves τa per tile, and interpolates retrieved atmospheric parameters to the full scene. 3. A "segmented" τa option, which computes a single fixed τa per lake polygon in the scene/subscene, see polylakes keyword. 4. An experimental "resolved" τa setting, which treats each pixel individually. This option is currently only included for development purposes. Note that processing time is much longer for this option.

claims.value: Sentinel-2 default: tiled DSF with 600 by 600 pixel tiles
claims.note: At 10 m this is 6 by 6 km. Manual section 4.5 lists fixed as default but says sensor defaults may differ. S2B and S2C files match.
claims.quote:
## dark spectrum fitting options
dsf_aot_estimate=tiled
dsf_spectrum_option=intercept
dsf_wave_range=400,900
s2_target_res=10
claims.locator: Lines 21 to 25, with dsf_tile_dimensions=600,600 at line 31

claims.value: Release 20221114.0 had the same tiled Sentinel-2 default
claims.note: dsf_tile_dimensions=600,600 at line 23 of the same file. Relevant if a product used that version.
claims.quote:
## dark spectrum fitting options
dsf_aot_estimate=tiled

claims.value: A region of one 600-pixel tile or less in either dimension falls back to fixed DSF
claims.note: Tile size is in pixels, so the threshold is 6 km at 10 m and 12 km at 20 m. Clips under that size run fixed.

claims.value: The aerosol estimate comes from the darkest pixels of the processed region or tile
claims.note: So the aerosol, and every rhos value, depends on the window processed. A clip and a whole-tile run can differ.
claims.quote: The DSF uses the bands and pixels giving the lowest estimate of aerosol optical thickness over the processed region or tile.
claims.locator: Section 2.2.2 'Glint correction', first sentence of second paragraph, PDF page 2

claims.value: Developer: tiles of mostly land or cloud can overestimate aerosol
claims.note: Reply in a 2024-07-16 forum thread about tile size over a narrow lagoon. The reply calls 6 by 6 km tiles probably fine.
claims.quote: You can use smaller tiles, but not that there may be issues near tiles containing mostly land or clouds. In those tiles the aerosol optical depth may be overestimated and the interpolation of the atmospheric correction parameters across such tiles may lead to poor results.
claims.locator: Reply by the ACOLITE developer account, posted 2024-07-16T05:11:31+00:00

claims.value: Sun glint remains in rhos unless the SWIR-based glint correction runs
claims.note: The alternative glint method works only with fixed aerosol, per the same paragraph.
claims.quote: The sun glint signal will however still be present in the resulting surface reflectance. A sun glint correction option is included, which by default uses the SWIR bands to estimate the glint signal, as in Harmel et al. (2018).
claims.locator: Section 2.2.2 'Glint correction', second paragraph, PDF page 2

claims.value: Residual glint correction is off by default, with default or alternative methods
claims.note: config/defaults.txt line 351 also sets False, and the Sentinel-2 defaults do not override it. An angle-based automatic option, dsf_residual_glint_correction_glint_angle, is off by default.
claims.quote: dsf_residual_glint_correction=False Controls the residual glint correction. Options: True/False dsf_residual_glint_correction_method=default Residual glint correction method to use. Options: default/alternative

claims.value: Air-water interface reflectance correction is off by default
claims.note: The reason given is sensitivity to local wind speed near nadir.
claims.quote: dsf_interface_reflectance=False Controls the air-water interface reflectance correction. Disabled by default at the moment since the surface reflectance is quite sensitive to (local) wind speed in nadir viewing conditions. Options: True/False

claims.value: Developer advice for single lakes: one run per lake, limited ROI, fixed DSF
claims.note: Forum reply of 2025-12-15 in a RAdCor thread about lakes of 3 to 22 ha. It means a single fixed aerosol estimate per lake window, not a user-set aerosol value.
claims.quote: My general recommendation for processing individual lakes with ACOLITE/DSF is to process them separately with a limited ROI covering the lake and a fixed aerosol (dsf_aot_estimate=fixed). For ACOLITE/RAdCor we have made the same recommendation. If the ROI is too large (or in your case, uses the full tile), TSDSF/DSF will find a target that is maybe too dark for the lake you are looking at.
claims.locator: Reply by the ACOLITE developer account, posted 2025-12-15T05:56:01+00:00, second paragraph

claims.value: Developer: whole-scene tiled DSF approximates per-target runs
claims.note: Same reply. It also warns that very bright tiles, such as clouds, distort neighbors through interpolation.
claims.quote: In DSF the setting dsf_aot_estimate=tiled cuts up the scene in subscenes and estimates the aerosol for each subscene. These aerosol estimates are then interpolated between the tiles, and the results should approximate those obtained when processing individual targets.
claims.locator: Reply by the ACOLITE developer account, posted 2025-12-15T05:56:01+00:00, third paragraph

claims.value: Segmented DSF gives one aerosol per lake polygon in a single run
claims.note: Manual section 4.5 calls segmented experimental. The polylakes keyword uses global lake databases, worldlakes or hydrolakes.
claims.quote: 3. A "segmented" τa option, which computes a single fixed τa per lake polygon in the scene/subscene, see polylakes keyword.

claims.value: Per-lake runs grow with lakes per tile-date, but one tiled or segmented run does not
claims.note: Unmeasured. A whole-tile run at 10 m needs much memory, per the developer reply in cl-wf-acolite-self-run-scaling_history-2.
claims.reasoning: The advised per-lake runs repeat conversion and aerosol fitting for every lake on the same local product. A tiled or segmented whole-tile run pays tile-sized compute once per tile-date.

claims.value: Linear in tile-dates: one whole Level-1C product staged and one run per date
claims.note: Unmeasured. No page gives run time or disk use per scene.
claims.reasoning: ACOLITE corrects one local Level-1C product per scene, or first downloads the whole product from CDSE. History cost therefore grows with the number of tile-dates.

claims.value: Developer: 10 m Sentinel-2 runs use a lot of memory
claims.note: Forum reply of 2024-04-17 on a full-tile run. It suggests 20 or 60 m output on a laptop. No figure is given. Each date in a history pays this cost.
claims.quote: Yes processing MSI data at 10 m resolution currently uses a lot of memory. For processing on a laptop I would suggest adapting the resolution of the MSI output products, e.g. s2_target_res=20 or s2_target_res=60.
claims.locator: First reply by the ACOLITE developer account, posted 2024-04-17T08:37:22+00:00

claims.value: Keeping L2R data in memory for L2W can exhaust RAM on large scenes
claims.note: The manual lists True, but config/defaults.txt line 257 sets l2w_data_in_memory=False.
claims.quote: l2w_data_in_memory=True Whether to load L2R data fully in memory when computing L2W data. When L2R data is kept into memory, L2W processing may be slightly faster at the cost of memory use. L2W processing for large scenes may run out of RAM with this option enabled. Options: True/False

claims.value: No scheduler required, and Docker images exist for parallel runs
claims.note: Images acolite/acolite:all_latest and tact_latest on DockerHub. Parallelism is left to the operator.
claims.quote: ACOLITE can be installed in a Docker container for deploying and running the processing in parallel.

questions_answered: Q1 inputs: Sentinel-2 Level-1C only, as a local .SAFE or a Level-1C Zarr. Level-2A is rejected for correction. A Sen2Cor converter only reformats Level-2A to NetCDF.
Q2 access: local .SAFE folders, zip or tar archives extracted first, or HTTPS Zarr URLs. An optional helper downloads whole products from CDSE. No AWS Sentinel-2 reader exists.
Q3 region: limit takes S, W, N, E degrees. polygon takes a file or WKT. Its envelope crops by default, and polygon_clip masks outside the outline.
Q3 partial reads: bands go through an in-memory GDAL warp to the region bounds. No page documents partial reads, and the product must be local.
Q4 aerosol: modes fixed, tiled, segmented, resolved, optimise, ancillary, and ancillary_fixed. The Sentinel-2 default is tiled with 600-pixel tiles.
Q4 leading claim, part one, confirmed: the estimate comes from the processed region or tile. A clip of 600 pixels or less in either dimension runs fixed automatically.
Q4 leading claim, part two, corrected: the developer advises one limited ROI per lake with dsf_aot_estimate=fixed. That estimates one aerosol per lake window. It does not set a user aerosol value.
Q4 also: the developer says whole-scene tiled results approximate per-target runs. No page gives a measured difference between a clipped run and a whole-tile run.
Q5 glint: dsf_residual_glint_correction=False and dsf_interface_reflectance=False by default. An angle-based automatic glint option arrived in 20260421.0, off by default.
Q6 outputs: NetCDF L1R with rhot, L2R with rhos, and L2W with rhow, Rrs, and others. GeoTIFF export is optional, one file per dataset. All bands share one 10, 20, or 60 m grid.
Q7 software: GPL-3.0, Python 3, conda-forge with GDAL JPEG 2000. Latest release 20260421.0 dated 2026-04-21. Release 20221114.0 exists, dated 2022-11-14.
Q8 resources: no page gives a run time, memory, or disk figure. The developer says 10 m runs use a lot of memory.
questions_open: Does GDAL read only the JPEG 2000 tiles a clip needs from a local SAFE? Test: time and trace one clipped run against a full-tile run on one product.
How large is the aerosol difference between a per-lake fixed run and a whole-tile tiled run on pilot lakes? Test: run both on a few pilot tile-dates.
Does segmented DSF accept user polygons through polygon and polygon_clip, or only polylakes databases? The code segments connected finite pixels. Test on one tile.
Can a Level-1C SAFE be staged from the AWS Level-1C bucket in a layout ACOLITE accepts? Not checked here. It needs a separate access-route check.
Which ACOLITE version and settings does the USGS product use? Its settings would set the target for a consistent gap fill. Phase B work.
What are run time, peak memory, and disk per scene at 20 m on a clip and on a full tile? No page gives them. Measure.
observations: The output pixel grid is the tile's UTM projection at s2_target_res. projection_sub.py snaps crop bounds to the scene pixel grid. A checker reading code can confirm this.
With polygon_clip=True, pixels outside the polygons become NaN before DSF runs. The dark spectrum then comes only from water pixels. This is a code reading, not tested.
The GEE module holds a gsutil helper that copies SAFE folders from Google Cloud Storage. The manual does not document it for normal runs.
A USGS contributor appears in the modification history of polygon_limit.py. This suggests USGS involvement in the code, not a documented USGS configuration.
Manual section 4.5 lists dsf_aot_estimate=fixed as default. The Sentinel-2 defaults files set tiled. Sensor defaults take precedence, as the manual states.
The developer recommends minimal settings files over copies of defaults.txt, because copies override sensor defaults.
A forum user reports a fixed-aerosol run on a small lake still underestimated aerosol against CAMS. One user's comparison, not evidence.

not_assessed.name: RAdCor adjacency correction (ACOLITE option)
not_assessed.why: An alternative ACOLITE method recommended for small inland waters. It is a setting of this candidate, not assessed separately here.

not_assessed.name: Sen2Cor Level-2A
not_assessed.why: ACOLITE has a converter for Sen2Cor products but does not correct them. Sen2Cor is the other source option, covered elsewhere.

not_assessed.name: T-Mart adjacency correction
not_assessed.why: Named by a forum user in comparison with RAdCor. No page for it was read.

not_assessed.name: SNAP gpt geometry
not_assessed.why: Optional geometry_type=gpt uses SNAP to compute view angles. It is a sub-option, not a processor candidate.

not_assessed.name: SeaDAS l2gen
not_assessed.why: Cited in the manual references and handled by an ACOLITE NetCDF converter. Not a Sentinel-2 workflow candidate here.

limitations: No Sentinel-2 data was read and ACOLITE was not run. Every claim comes from the manual, the README, defaults files, source code, release pages, or forum posts.
Source code claims cite the main branch at commit ca477dd, dated 2026-10-07. That is later than release 20260421.0. Line numbers apply to that commit only.
The manual is a PDF. Quotes join wrapped lines with single spaces and remove line-end hyphens, as in 'surface'. Greek symbols follow the PDF text layer.
No ACOLITE page documents whether a clipped run reads only part of each band file. read_pattern-11 cites code only. GDAL behavior on local JPEG 2000 was not checked.
No page gives run time, memory, or disk figures per scene. The only resource statements are qualitative developer replies and one manual note on RAM.
The developer's small-lake advice appears in forum replies, not in the manual. Forum posts can change or vanish. Timestamps in locators identify the replies.
The Optics Express sensitivity paper (doi 10.1364/OE.397456) was blocked by a bot check. Its region-size findings, quoted second hand in a forum post, are not used.
acolite.readthedocs.io hosts a 'User Guide' labeled version 20240101.0, which is not a release. Its publisher is unclear, so it was not used.
POLYMER, C2RCC, and iCOR did not appear on any cited page. They are not listed in not_assessed.
The leading claim on window dependence is confirmed in mechanism only. No page reports the size of the difference between clipped and whole-tile runs.
